def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    if not adj:
        return []
    n = len(adj)
    if n == 1:
        return [0]

    # Detect if input is adjacency matrix (square with 0/1 entries)
    is_matrix = False
    if len(adj[0]) == n:
        if all(all(x in (0, 1) for x in row) for row in adj):
            is_matrix = True

    # Build adjacency list and bitmask representation
    if is_matrix:
        adj_list = [[j for j in range(n) if adj[i][j] == 1] for i in range(n)]
    else:
        adj_list = [list(neigh) for neigh in adj]  # copy to avoid mutation

    bit_adj = [0] * n
    for u in range(n):
        mask = 0
        for v in adj_list[u]:
            mask |= 1 << v
        bit_adj[u] = mask

    # Helper: compute degree in subgraph induced by uncolored vertices
    def degree_in_uncolored(v, uncolored_set):
        return (bit_adj[v] & uncolored_set).bit_count()

    # DSATUR with degree tie-breaking
    def dsatur():
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored_set = (1 << n) - 1
        saturation = [0] * n  # number of distinct colors in neighborhood
        neighbor_colors = [0] * n  # bitmask of colors used by neighbors

        for _ in range(n):
            # Select uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree in uncolored subgraph
            best_v = -1
            best_sat = -1
            best_deg = -1
            for v in range(n):
                if color[v] == -1:
                    sat = saturation[v]
                    deg = degree_in_uncolored(v, uncolored_set)
                    if sat > best_sat or (sat == best_sat and deg > best_deg):
                        best_sat = sat
                        best_deg = deg
                        best_v = v
            v = best_v

            # Find smallest available color
            used = neighbor_colors[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c

            # Update uncolored set and neighbor info
            uncolored_set &= ~(1 << v)
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] == -1:  # only update uncolored neighbors
                    neighbor_colors[u] |= (1 << c)
                    saturation[u] = neighbor_colors[u].bit_count()
        return color

    # RLF (Recursive Largest First) independent set extraction
    def rlf():
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored_set = (1 << n) - 1
        c = 0
        while uncolored_set:
            # Build independent set S for color c
            S = 0  # bitmask of vertices in current independent set
            W = 0  # vertices adjacent to S (ineligible)
            # Choose vertex with max degree in uncolored subgraph
            v = -1
            max_deg = -1
            temp = uncolored_set
            while temp:
                lsb = temp & -temp
                i = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                deg = degree_in_uncolored(i, uncolored_set)
                if deg > max_deg:
                    max_deg = deg
                    v = i
                temp ^= lsb
            if v == -1:  # should not happen
                break
            S |= (1 << v)
            W |= bit_adj[v] & uncolored_set  # neighbors of v in uncolored
            U = uncolored_set & ~S & ~W  # eligible vertices

            while U:
                # Select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|, tie-break by min degree in U
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_deg_u = -1
                temp = U
                while temp:
                    lsb = temp & -temp
                    u = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                    # score = number of neighbors in W
                    score = (bit_adj[u] & W).bit_count()
                    deg_u = degree_in_uncolored(u, U)
                    if score > best_score or (score == best_score and deg_u < best_deg_u):
                        best_score = score
                        best_deg_u = deg_u
                        best_u = u
                    temp ^= lsb
                u = best_u
                S |= (1 << u)
                # Move u from U, add its neighbors in U to W
                nbrs_in_U = bit_adj[u] & U
                W |= nbrs_in_U
                U &= ~((1 << u) | nbrs_in_U)
            # Assign color c to all vertices in S
            temp = S
            while temp:
                lsb = temp & -temp
                i = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                color[i] = c
                temp ^= lsb
            # Remove S from uncolored, set uncolored to W for next color
            uncolored_set = W
            c += 1
        return color

        order = []
        remaining = set(range(n))

        current_adj = [set(neigh) for neigh in adj_list]

            v = -1
            min_deg = math.inf
            for u in remaining:
                d = len(current_adj[u] & remaining)
                if d < min_deg:
                    min_deg = d
                    v = u
            order.append(v)
            remaining.remove(v)
            # remove v from adjacency sets
            for u in current_adj[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    current_adj[u].discard(v)
        # Color in reverse order
        color = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << color[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
        return color

    candidates = []
    candidates.append(dsatur())
    candidates.append(rlf())
    candidates.append(smallest_last())

    best_color = None
    best_k = math.inf
    for col in candidates:

        if _is_valid_coloring(col, bit_adj):

            if k < best_k:

    if best_color is None:

    improved = _kempe_reduce(best_color, bit_adj, n)

def _is_valid_coloring(color, bit_adj):
    n = len(color)
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (bit_adj[u] >> v) & 1:  # edge exists
                if color[u] == color[v]:
                    return False
    return True

def _compact_colors(color):
    # Map colors to 0..k-1 preserving order of first appearance
    mapping = {}
    next_color = 0
    compacted = []
    for c in color:
        if c not in mapping:
            mapping[c] = next_color
            next_color += 1
        compacted.append(mapping[c])
    return compacted

            for u in adj_list_from_bit(bit_adj, u=n):  # inefficient, but n<=100
                if color[u] != -1:
                    neighbor_colors |= (1 << color[u])
            # Actually, we need adj_list; we'll compute from bit_adj on the fly
            # Recompute neighbor colors for v
            neighbor_colors = 0
            mask = bit_adj[v]
            while mask:
                lsb = mask & -mask

                if color[u] != -1:
                    neighbor_colors |= (1 << color[u])
                mask ^= lsb
            for c in range(target_color):
                if not (neighbor_colors & (1 << c)):
                    # can recolor v to c
                    color[v] = c
                    made_change = True
                    break
            if made_change:
                break  # restart from highest color after any change
            # Try Kempe chains with each lower color
            for c in range(target_color):
                if neighbor_colors & (1 << c):
                    # both colors present in neighborhood, try Kempe chain
                    # We'll try to swap in the component of v for (target_color, c)
                    # if we can recolor v to c without increasing target_color count
                    visited = [False] * n
                    stack = [v]
                    visited[v] = True
                    component = []
                    while stack:
                        node = stack.pop()
                        component.append(node)
                        for u in adj_list_from_bit(bit_adj, n):
                            if color[u] == target_color or color[u] == c:
                                if not visited[u]:
                                    visited[u] = True
                                    stack.append(u)
                    # Check if any neighbor of the component has color c (would block)
                    # Actually, we can swap if no vertex in component adjacent to outside c?
                    # Standard: swapping is always valid; we just want to eliminate target_color
                    # So we swap and see if we reduce the number of vertices with target_color
                    # Swap colors in component
                    for node in component:
                        if color[node] == target_color:
                            color[node] = c
                        elif color[node] == c:
                            color[node] = target_color
                    # Count how many vertices still have target_color
                    new_count = sum(1 for i in range(n) if color[i] == target_color)
                    if new_count < len(verts):  # we reduced the count
                        made_change = True
                        break
                    else:
                        # swap back
                        for node in component:
                            if color[node] == target_color:
                                color[node] = c
                            elif color[node] == c:
                                color[node] = target_color
                if made_change:
                    break
            if made_change:
                break
        if not made_change:
            # cannot eliminate this color, try next lower
            continue
        else:
            # we made a change, restart from highest color
            return _kempe_reduce(color, bit_adj, n)  # recurse
    # If we get here, no improvement possible
    return color

def adj_list_from_bit(bit_adj, n):
    # Helper to get adjacency list from bitmask (for small n)
    adj_list = []
    for u in range(n):
        neighbors = []
        mask = bit_adj[u]
        while mask:
            lsb = mask & -mask
            v = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
            neighbors.append(v)
            mask ^= lsb
        adj_list.append(neighbors)
    return adj_list

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    if not adj:
        return []
    n = len(adj)
    # Detect adjacency matrix vs list
    if len(adj[0]) == n and all(isinstance(x, int) and x in (0, 1) for row in adj for x in row):
        # adjacency matrix
        bit_adj = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j]:
                    bit_adj[i] |= 1 << j
        degree = [row.count(1) for row in adj]
    else:
        # adjacency list
        bit_adj = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            for j in adj[i]:
                bit_adj[i] |= 1 << j
        degree = [len(adj[i]) for i in range(n)]

    # Helper: greedy coloring given an ordering
    def greedy_color(order):
        color = [-1] * n
        used = [0] * n  # bitmask of colors used by neighbors
        for v in order:
            c = 0
            while used[v] & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            # update neighbors
            mask = bit_adj[v]
            u = 0
            while mask:
                if mask & 1:
                    used[u] |= 1 << c
                mask >>= 1
                u += 1
        return color

    # Helper: number of colors used
    def num_colors(coloring):
        return max(coloring) + 1 if coloring else 0

    # Helper: validate coloring
    def is_valid(coloring):
        for u in range(n):
            mask = bit_adj[u]
            v = 0
            while mask:
                if mask & 1:
                    if coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
                        return False
                mask >>= 1
                v += 1
        return True

    # DSATUR
    def dsatur():
        color = [-1] * n
        sat = [0] * n  # saturation degree
        colored = [False] * n
        # neighbor color masks
        neighbor_colors = [0] * n
        for _ in range(n):
            # select uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree
            v = -1
            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in range(n):
                if not colored[u]:
                    if sat[u] > max_sat or (sat[u] == max_sat and degree[u] > max_deg):
                        max_sat = sat[u]
                        max_deg = degree[u]
                        v = u
            if v == -1:
                break  # should not happen
            # find smallest available color
            c = 0
            while neighbor_colors[v] & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            colored[v] = True
            # update saturation of neighbors
            mask = bit_adj[v]
            u = 0
            while mask:
                if mask & 1:
                    if not colored[u]:
                        # add color c to neighbor's palette
                        if not (neighbor_colors[u] & (1 << c)):
                            neighbor_colors[u] |= 1 << c
                            sat[u] += 1
                mask >>= 1
                u += 1
        return color

    # RLF (Recursive Largest First)
    def rlf():
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        c = 0
        while uncolored:
            # build independent set for color c
            # start with vertex of max degree in uncolored subgraph
            # compute degrees in uncolored subgraph
            deg_sub = {}
            for v in uncolored:
                cnt = 0
                mask = bit_adj[v]
                u = 0
                while mask:
                    if mask & 1 and u in uncolored:
                        cnt += 1
                    mask >>= 1
                    u += 1
                deg_sub[v] = cnt
            # pick v with max degree in subgraph
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: deg_sub[x])
            S = {v}
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # U: vertices not adjacent to any in S
            # W: vertices adjacent to at least one in S
            W = set()
            for u in list(uncolored):
                if bit_adj[v] & (1 << u):
                    W.add(u)
            U = uncolored - W
            while U:
                # select u in U with max neighbors in W
                best_u = -1
                max_w_neighbors = -1
                min_deg_u = float('inf')
                for u in U:
                    # count neighbors in W
                    w_cnt = 0
                    mask = bit_adj[u]
                    w = 0
                    while mask:
                        if mask & 1 and w in W:
                            w_cnt += 1
                        mask >>= 1
                        w += 1
                    # tie-break: min degree in U-induced subgraph
                    deg_u = 0
                    mask2 = bit_adj[u]
                    w2 = 0
                    while mask2:
                        if mask2 & 1 and w2 in U:
                            deg_u += 1
                        mask2 >>= 1
                        w2 += 1
                    if w_cnt > max_w_neighbors or (w_cnt == max_w_neighbors and deg_u < min_deg_u):
                        max_w_neighbors = w_cnt
                        min_deg_u = deg_u
                        best_u = u
                if best_u == -1:
                    break
                S.add(best_u)
                uncolored.remove(best_u)
                # move neighbors of best_u from U to W
                mask = bit_adj[best_u]
                w = 0
                while mask:
                    if mask & 1 and w in U:
                        U.remove(w)
                        W.add(w)
                    mask >>= 1
                    w += 1
                U.discard(best_u)
            # assign color c to all in S
            for v in S:
                color[v] = c
            c += 1
        return color

    # Smallest-Last ordering (Matula & Beck)
    def smallest_last():
        # core decomposition to get ordering
        deg = degree[:]
        visited = [False] * n
        order = []
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for v in range(n):
            if deg[v] < n:
                buckets[deg[v]].append(v)
        pos = 0
        for d in range(n):
            while buckets[d]:
                v = buckets[d].pop()
                if visited[v]:
                    continue
                visited[v] = True
                order.append(v)
                # decrease degree of unvisited neighbors
                mask = bit_adj[v]
                u = 0
                while mask:
                    if mask & 1 and not visited[u]:
                        if deg[u] > d:
                            deg[u] -= 1
                            buckets[deg[u]].append(u)
                    mask >>= 1
                    u += 1
        # color in reverse order
        return greedy_color(order[::-1])

    # Kempe chain color reduction
    def kempe_reduce(coloring):
        # make coloring consecutive
        def renorm(col):
            mapping = {}
            next_c = 0
            for v in range(n):
                c = col[v]
                if c not in mapping:
                    mapping[c] = next_c
                    next_c += 1
                col[v] = mapping[c]
            return col

        coloring = renorm(coloring[:])
        k = num_colors(coloring)
        improved = True
        while improved and k > 1:
            improved = False
            # target smallest color class (color k-1)
            target_color = k - 1
            vertices = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]
            if not vertices:
                k -= 1
                continue
            # try to recolor each vertex in target class
            for v in vertices:
                # try direct reassignment to a lower color
                neighbor_mask = 0
                mask = bit_adj[v]
                u = 0
                while mask:
                    if mask & 1:
                        neighbor_mask |= 1 << coloring[u]
                    mask >>= 1
                    u += 1
                for c in range(target_color):
                    if not (neighbor_mask & (1 << c)):
                        # move v to color c
                        coloring[v] = c
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:
                    break
                # try Kempe chains with each lower color
                for c in range(target_color):
                    # if v already can take c, skip (should have been caught)
                    if not (neighbor_mask & (1 << c)):
                        continue
                    # BFS to find (c, target_color) Kempe chain containing v
                    from collections import deque
                    visited_k = [False] * n
                    queue = deque([v])
                    visited_k[v] = True
                    component = []
                    while queue:
                        x = queue.popleft()
                        component.append(x)
                        mask = bit_adj[x]
                        y = 0
                        while mask:
                            if mask & 1:
                                if coloring[y] == c or coloring[y] == target_color:
                                    if not visited_k[y]:
                                        visited_k[y] = True
                                        queue.append(y)
                            mask >>= 1
                            y += 1
                    # check if we can swap: after swap, no neighbor of v has color c
                    # actually, swapping will give v color c, so we need that no neighbor has color c after swap
                    # but neighbors that are c become target_color, and vice versa.
                    # so we need that no neighbor of v is colored c in the current coloring (because they will become target_color)
                    # wait: after swap, v becomes c. Its neighbors that were c become target_color, so no conflict.
                    # neighbors that were target_color become c -> conflict if they are adjacent to v? 
                    # Actually, if a neighbor u of v is target_color, after swap it becomes c, same as v -> conflict.
                    # Therefore, we can only swap if v has no neighbor colored target_color in the component? 
                    # Let's think: we are swapping colors c and target_color in the component.
                    # For any edge inside the component, if endpoints have different colors, they swap -> still different.
                    # For edges from component to outside: 
                    #   if outside vertex colored c, and inside vertex colored target_color -> after swap, inside becomes c -> conflict.
                    #   similarly, if outside colored target_color and inside colored c -> after swap inside becomes target_color -> conflict.
                    # So swapping is safe only if there is no edge from the component to a vertex colored c or target_color outside.
                    # But we can check: for the component, if there is no neighbor of any vertex in the component that is colored c (outside) and no neighbor colored target_color (outside)? 
                    # Actually, we only need that after swap, v does not conflict. v will be color c.
                    # So we need that no neighbor of v is colored c after swap.
                    # Neighbors of v that are in the component: if they were c, they become target_color; if they were target_color, they become c.
                    # So after swap, neighbors of v in component that were target_color become c -> same as v -> conflict.
                    # Therefore, to avoid conflict, v must have no neighbor in the component that is colored target_color.
                    # But v is in the component and colored target_color, so if there is another vertex in component adjacent to v and colored target_color, then after swap both become c -> conflict.
                    # Actually, the component is connected via alternating colors, so there might be such a neighbor.
                    # Instead, we can check: after swap, for each neighbor u of v, what color does it have?
                    #   if u in component: 
                    #       if coloring[u] == c -> becomes target_color
                    #       if coloring[u] == target_color -> becomes c
                    #   else: remains coloring[u]
                    # So v becomes c. Conflict if any neighbor u has color c after swap.
                    #   => if u in component and coloring[u] == target_color (becomes c) -> conflict
                    #   => if u not in component and coloring[u] == c -> conflict
                    safe = True
                    mask = bit_adj[v]
                    u = 0
                    while mask:
                        if mask & 1:
                            if visited_k[u]:  # u in component
                                if coloring[u] == target_color:
                                    safe = False
                                    break
                            else:  # u not in component
                                if coloring[u] == c:
                                    safe = False
                                    break
                        mask >>= 1
                        u += 1
                    if safe:
                        # perform swap
                        for x in component:
                            if coloring[x] == c:
                                coloring[x] = target_color
                            elif coloring[x] == target_color:
                                coloring[x] = c
                        improved = True
                        break
            if improved:
                coloring = renorm(coloring)
                k = num_colors(coloring)
        return coloring

    # Run all heuristics
    candidates = []
    try:
        c1 = dsatur()
        if is_valid(c1):
            candidates.append(c1)
    except:
        pass
    try:
        c2 = rlf()
        if is_valid(c2):
            candidates.append(c2)
    except:
        pass
    try:
        c3 = smallest_last()
        if is_valid(c3):
            candidates.append(c3)
    except:
        pass

    # Also try greedy with degree order
    try:
        order_deg = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: degree[x], reverse=True)
        c4 = greedy_color(order_deg)
        if is_valid(c4):
            candidates.append(c4)
    except:
        pass

    # If no candidates, fallback to trivial
    if not candidates:
        coloring = [0] * n
        for i in range(1, n):
            if any(bit_adj[i] & (1 << j) and coloring[j] == 0 for j in range(i)):
                coloring[i] = 1
        candidates.append(coloring)

    # Select best (fewest colors)
    best = min(candidates, key=num_colors)
    best = kempe_reduce(best)
    # Final validation and renorm
    if not is_valid(best):
        # last resort: greedy with DSATUR order
        best = dsatur()
    return renorm(best)

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    """
    Colors an undirected graph with the minimum number of colors using a hybrid approach
    combining DSATUR, RLF, Smallest-Last, and Kempe chain refinement.
    """
    n = len(adj)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    if n == 1:
        return [0]

    # Detect input format: adjacency matrix or adjacency list
    is_matrix = False
    if len(adj) > 0 and len(adj[0]) == len(adj):
        # Check if it's a binary matrix
        is_matrix = True
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                val = adj[i][j]
                if val != 0 and val != 1:
                    is_matrix = False
                    break
            if not is_matrix:
                break
        if is_matrix:
            # Validate symmetry and zero diagonal (undirected simple graph)
            for i in range(n):
                if adj[i][i] != 0:
                    is_matrix = False
                    break
                for j in range(i + 1, n):
                    if adj[i][j] != adj[j][i]:
                        is_matrix = False
                        break
                if not is_matrix:
                    break

    # Build adjacency list and bitmask representation
    adj_list = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    bit_adj = [0] * n
    if is_matrix:
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1:
                    adj_list[i].append(j)
                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
    else:
        # Treat as adjacency list
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj[u]:
                if v < 0 or v >= n:
                    continue  # Skip invalid indices
                adj_list[u].append(v)
                bit_adj[u] |= (1 << v)
        # Ensure undirected: add reverse edges if missing
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u not in adj_list[v]:
                    adj_list[v].append(u)
                    bit_adj[v] |= (1 << u)

    # Helper: compute degree in the subgraph induced by a set of vertices (given as bitmask)
    def degree_in_set(u: int, mask: int) -> int:
        return (bit_adj[u] & mask).bit_count()

    # Helper: greedy coloring with a given vertex order
    def greedy_color(order: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        color = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            # Compute neighbor colors
            neighbor_colors = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:
                    neighbor_colors |= (1 << color[u])
            # Find smallest non-negative integer not in neighbor_colors (mex)
            c = 0
            while neighbor_colors & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
        return color

    # Helper: count number of colors used
    def num_colors(coloring: list[int]) -> int:
        if not coloring:
            return 0
        return max(coloring) + 1

    # Helper: check if coloring is valid
    def is_valid(coloring: list[int]) -> bool:
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
                    return False
        return True

    # Strategy 1: DSATUR with degree tie-breaking
    def dsatur() -> list[int]:
        color = [-1] * n
        # saturation[v] = bitmask of colors used by colored neighbors
        saturation = [0] * n
        # Track uncolored vertices
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        # Start with vertex of highest degree
        if uncolored:
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: len(adj_list[x]))
            color[v] = 0
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # Update saturation for neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in uncolored:
                    saturation[u] |= (1 << 0)
        # Main loop
        while uncolored:
            # Select vertex with max saturation, break ties by degree in uncolored subgraph, then random
            best_v = -1
            best_sat = -1
            best_deg = -1
            for v in uncolored:
                sat = saturation[v].bit_count()
                deg = degree_in_set(v, sum(1 << u for u in uncolored))
                if sat > best_sat or (sat == best_sat and deg > best_deg) or (sat == best_sat and deg == best_deg and random.random() < 0.5):
                    best_sat = sat
                    best_deg = deg
                    best_v = v
            v = best_v
            # Find smallest available color
            neighbor_colors = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:
                    neighbor_colors |= (1 << color[u])
            c = 0
            while neighbor_colors & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # Update saturation for neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in uncolored:
                    saturation[u] |= (1 << c)
        return color

    # Strategy 2: RLF (Recursive Largest First)
    def rlf() -> list[int]:
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored_mask = (1 << n) - 1  # bitmask of uncolored vertices
        c = 0
        while uncolored_mask:
            # Build maximal independent set for color c
            independent_set = 0  # bitmask
            # Step 1: pick vertex of max degree in uncolored subgraph
            v = -1
            max_deg = -1
            temp = uncolored_mask
            while temp:
                u = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                deg = degree_in_set(u, uncolored_mask)
                if deg > max_deg:
                    max_deg = deg
                    v = u
                temp &= temp - 1
            if v == -1:  # should not happen
                break
            independent_set |= (1 << v)
            # Partition uncolored vertices into U (not adj to S) and W (adj to S)
            # W = neighbors of independent_set within uncolored
            W = 0
            temp_inds = independent_set
            while temp_inds:
                u = (temp_inds & -temp_inds).bit_length() - 1
                W |= bit_adj[u]
                temp_inds &= temp_inds - 1
            W &= uncolored_mask  # only uncolored neighbors
            U = uncolored_mask & ~W & ~independent_set  # uncolored, not in S, not adj to S
            # Main loop: while U not empty
            while U:
                # Select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|, tie-break by min degree in U
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_deg_u = -1
                temp = U
                while temp:
                    u = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                    # score = |N(u) ∩ W|
                    neighbors_in_W = (bit_adj[u] & W).bit_count()
                    deg_u = degree_in_set(u, U)
                    if neighbors_in_W > best_score or (neighbors_in_W == best_score and deg_u < best_deg_u) or \
                       (neighbors_in_W == best_score and deg_u == best_deg_u and random.random() < 0.5):
                        best_score = neighbors_in_W
                        best_deg_u = deg_u
                        best_u = u
                    temp &= temp - 1
                u = best_u
                # Add u to independent set
                independent_set |= (1 << u)
                # Move u from U to W? Actually, remove u from U, and add its neighbors in U to W
                U &= ~(1 << u)
                # Add neighbors of u that are in U to W
                neighbors_in_U = bit_adj[u] & U
                W |= neighbors_in_U
                # Remove those neighbors from U (since they are now adjacent to S)
                U &= ~neighbors_in_U
            # Assign color c to all vertices in independent_set
            temp = independent_set
            while temp:
                v = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                color[v] = c
                temp &= temp - 1
            # Update uncolored_mask: remove independent_set
            uncolored_mask &= ~independent_set
            c += 1
        return color

    # Strategy 3: Smallest-Last ordering (Matula & Beck)
    def smallest_last() -> list[int]:
        # Compute degeneracy ordering by repeatedly removing min degree vertex
        deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        removed = [False] * n
        order = []  # removal order
        # We'll use buckets for efficiency (since n <= 100, simple scan is fine)
        for _ in range(n):
            # Find vertex with minimum degree among non-removed
            min_deg = float('inf')
            v = -1
            for i in range(n):
                if not removed[i] and deg[i] < min_deg:
                    min_deg = deg[i]
                    v = i
            if v == -1:
                break  # should not happen
            removed[v] = True
            order.append(v)
            # Update degrees of neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if not removed[u]:
                    deg[u] -= 1
        # Color in reverse removal order
        return greedy_color(order[::-1])

    # Strategy 4: Welsh-Powell (sort by degree descending)
    def welsh_powell() -> list[int]:
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(adj_list[x]), reverse=True)
        return greedy_color(order)

    # Run all strategies and collect valid colorings
    start_time = time.time()
    strategies = [
        ("DSATUR", dsatur),
        ("RLF", rlf),
        ("Smallest-Last", smallest_last),
        ("Welsh-Powell", welsh_powell)
    ]
    best_coloring = None
    best_k = float('inf')
    for name, func in strategies:
        # Timeout check
        if time.time() - start_time > 0.04:  # leave time for refinement
            break
        coloring = func()
        if is_valid(coloring):
            k = num_colors(coloring)
            if k < best_k:
                best_k = k
                best_coloring = coloring[:]
        # If we already have a 1-coloring (only possible for edgeless), we can't do better
        if best_k == 1:
            break

    # If no valid coloring found (should not happen), fall back to greedy on natural order
    if best_coloring is None:
        best_coloring = greedy_color(list(range(n)))
        best_k = num_colors(best_coloring)

    # Kempe chain-based color reduction
    def eliminate_color_class(coloring: list[int], target_color: int) -> list[int] | None:
        """
        Attempt to eliminate target_color by recoloring its vertices.
        Returns a new coloring with target_color removed if successful, else None.
        """
        n_local = len(coloring)
        # Get vertices with target_color
        target_vertices = [v for v in range(n_local) if coloring[v] == target_color]
        if not target_vertices:
            return coloring  # already eliminated

        # Try direct reassignment: can any target vertex take a lower color?
        for v in target_vertices:
            used = [False] * (target_color)  # only need to check colors < target_color
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                c = coloring[u]
                if c < target_color:
                    used[c] = True
            for c in range(target_color):
                if not used[c]:
                    # Recolor v to c
                    new_coloring = coloring[:]
                    new_coloring[v] = c
                    return new_coloring

        # Try Kempe chain swaps for each pair (target_color, c) where c < target_color
        for c in range(target_color):
            # Build subgraph induced by colors c and target_color
            # We'll try to find a Kempe chain that, when swapped, frees color c for some target vertex
            # without introducing conflicts.
            # For each vertex v in target_vertices, check if v is not connected to any c-colored vertex
            # in its Kempe chain component (so swapping won't pull a c-colored vertex into target_color)
            # Actually, we want: after swapping the component containing v, v becomes c, and we need
            # to ensure that no neighbor of v is c after swap (which would be a conflict).
            # But swapping only changes c<->target_color in the component.
            # So, if we swap the component containing v, then:
            #   - v becomes c
            #   - any neighbor of v that was in the component and had color c becomes target_color
            #   - any neighbor of v that was in the component and had target_color becomes c
            #   - neighbors outside the component keep their color.
            # For v to be safely recolored to c, we need that after swap, no neighbor of v has color c.
            # Neighbors of v that are c after swap come from:
            #   - neighbors originally colored target_color that are in the same component as v (they become c)
            #   - neighbors originally colored c that are NOT in the same component as v (they remain c)
            # So, to avoid conflict, we need:
            #   (1) No neighbor of v that is colored target_color is in the same Kempe component as v.
            #   (2) No neighbor of v that is colored c is outside the Kempe component of v.
            # But condition (2) is equivalent to: all neighbors of v that are colored c are in the same Kempe component as v.
            # However, it's easier to simulate: try swapping the component and check validity.
            # Since n is small, we can do BFS for each target vertex.

            # Precompute which vertices are of color c or target_color
            is_relevant = [False] * n_local
            for v in range(n_local):
                if coloring[v] == c or coloring[v] == target_color:

            for v in target_vertices:

                new_coloring = coloring[:]
                temp = comp_mask
                while temp:

                    if new_coloring[x] == c:

                    elif new_coloring[x] == target_color:
                        new_coloring[x] = c
                    temp &= temp - 1
                # Check if this new coloring is valid and has one less color (i.e., target_color is not used)
                if is_valid(new_coloring):

                    if target_color not in new_coloring:

                    # Even if not eliminated, we might have made progress? But we aim to eliminate.

    # Iteratively try to eliminate the smallest color class

        if new_coloring is not None:

        if not coloring:

        mask = 0

        neighbor_color_mask = [0] * n

    def rlf():

            W = set()
            for v in uncolored_set:

                U.remove(u)

                for v in list(U):  # iterate over copy

            # Assign color to all in S
            for v in S:
                coloring[v] = color

    # Handle trivial cases

            for u in range(n):

                        max_deg = deg_u

                    elif sat_u == max_sat and deg_u == max_deg and v == -1:

            # Find smallest available color (mex)
            used_colors = 0
            # Collect colors from colored neighbors
            nbr_mask = colored_neighbors_mask[v]
            while nbr_mask:
                # Extract lowest set bit

                color_idx = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                used_colors |= (1 << color_idx)
                nbr_mask ^= lsb
            # Find first zero bit in used_colors

                # If u is colored, no need to update anything for DSATUR selection
            uncolored_count -= 1

    # RLF algorithm (Recursive Largest First)

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

    is_matrix = False

        is_matrix = True

            for j in range(n):

                    is_matrix = False
                    break
            if not is_matrix:

            for j in range(n):

    for u in range(n):
        mask = 0
        for v in adj_list[u]:
            mask |= (1 << v)
        bit_adj[u] = mask

    def is_proper(coloring):
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
                    return False
        return True
    # Helper: number of colors used
    def num_colors(coloring):
        if not coloring:
            return 0
        return max(coloring) + 1
    # Helper: compact colors to 0..k-1
    def compact_colors(coloring):
        if not coloring:
            return coloring
        # Map used colors to 0..k-1
        used = set(coloring)
        mapping = {}
        for i, c in enumerate(sorted(used)):
            mapping[c] = i
        return [mapping[c] for c in coloring]
    # DSATUR
    def dsatur():
        color = [-1] * n
        # saturation: number of distinct colors in neighbors
        sat = [0] * n
        # neighbor color sets as bitmask
        neighbor_colors = [0] * n
        # degree in uncolored subgraph
        uncolored_deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        for _ in range(n):
            # select uncolored vertex with max sat, tie-break by max uncolored_deg, then min index
            v = -1
            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                if sat[u] > max_sat or (sat[u] == max_sat and uncolored_deg[u] > max_deg) or \
                   (sat[u] == max_sat and uncolored_deg[u] == max_deg and u < v):
                    max_sat = sat[u]
                    max_deg = uncolored_deg[u]
                    v = u
            # find smallest color not used by neighbors
            used = neighbor_colors[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            # update neighbors of v
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] == -1:  # u is uncolored
                    # update saturation if color c is new to u's neighbors
                    if not (neighbor_colors[u] & (1 << c)):
                        neighbor_colors[u] |= (1 << c)
                        sat[u] += 1
                    uncolored_deg[u] -= 1
            uncolored.remove(v)
        return color
    # RLF
    def rlf():
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        c = 0
        while uncolored:
            # find vertex with max degree in uncolored subgraph
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda u: sum(1 for w in adj_list[u] if w in uncolored))
            S = {v}
            # U: vertices not adjacent to any in S
            U = {u for u in uncolored if u != v and all(w not in adj_list[u] for w in S)}
            # W: vertices adjacent to at least one in S
            W = {u for u in uncolored if u not in S and u not in U}
            while U:
                # select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|
                u_star = -1
                max_common = -1
                min_deg_U = float('inf')
                for u in U:
                    common = sum(1 for w in adj_list[u] if w in W)
                    deg_U = sum(1 for w in adj_list[u] if w in U)
                    if common > max_common or (common == max_common and deg_U < min_deg_U) or \
                       (common == max_common and deg_U == min_deg_U and u < u_star):
                        max_common = common
                        min_deg_U = deg_U
                        u_star = u
                S.add(u_star)
                U.remove(u_star)

                for w in adj_list[u_star]:
                    if w in U:
                        U.remove(w)
                        W.add(w)

            for u in S:
                color[u] = c

            c += 1

        order = []

        deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        # bucket sort by degree

        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        for v in range(n):
            buckets[deg[v]].append(v)
        # pointer to current min degree
        min_deg = 0
        for _ in range(n):
            # find non-empty bucket
            while min_deg <= max_deg and not buckets[min_deg]:
                min_deg += 1
            if min_deg > max_deg:
                break
            v = buckets[min_deg].pop()
            order.append(v)
            remaining.remove(v)
            # update neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    d = deg[u]
                    buckets[d].remove(u)
                    deg[u] -= 1
                    buckets[deg[u]].append(u)
                    if deg[u] < min_deg:
                        min_deg = deg[u]
        # color in reverse order
        color = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << color[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
        return color
    # Kempe chain swap for colors a and b, returns new coloring if swap performed, else None
    def kempe_swap(coloring, a, b):
        n_local = len(coloring)
        # Build adjacency for colors a and b
        # Find vertices with color a or b
        ab_vertices = [i for i in range(n_local) if coloring[i] == a or coloring[i] == b]
        if not ab_vertices:
            return None
        # Build graph induced by these vertices
        # We'll do BFS to find components
        visited = [False] * n_local
        from collections import deque
        for start in ab_vertices:
            if visited[start]:
                continue
            # BFS to get component
            comp = []
            queue = deque([start])
            visited[start] = True
            while queue:
                u = queue.popleft()
                comp.append(u)
                for v in adj_list[u]:
                    if not visited[v] and (coloring[v] == a or coloring[v] == b):
                        visited[v] = True
                        queue.append(v)
            # Check if this component contains both colors a and b
            has_a = any(coloring[u] == a for u in comp)
            has_b = any(coloring[u] == b for u in comp)
            if has_a and has_b:
                # swap colors in this component
                new_coloring = coloring[:]
                for u in comp:
                    if new_coloring[u] == a:
                        new_coloring[u] = b
                    else:
                        new_coloring[u] = a
                return new_coloring
        return None
    # Try to reduce colors using Kempe chains
    def reduce_kempe(coloring):
        k = num_colors(coloring)
        if k <= 1:
            return coloring
        # Try to eliminate color classes from highest to lowest
        for target_color in range(k-1, 0, -1):
            # vertices with target_color
            verts = [i for i in range(n) if coloring[i] == target_color]
            if not verts:
                continue
            # Try to recolor each vertex
            changed = True
            while changed and verts:
                changed = False
                new_coloring = coloring[:]
                # Try direct reassignment first
                for v in verts[:]:
                    if new_coloring[v] != target_color:
                        continue
                    used = 0
                    for u in adj_list[v]:
                        if new_coloring[u] != -1:
                            used |= (1 << new_coloring[u])
                    # find smallest color not used
                    for c in range(target_color):  # only try lower colors
                        if not (used & (1 << c)):
                            new_coloring[v] = c
                            changed = True
                            break
                    if changed:
                        verts.remove(v)
                if changed:
                    coloring = new_coloring
                    continue
                # Try Kempe chains
                for v in verts[:]:
                    if new_coloring[v] != target_color:
                        continue
                    for c in range(target_color):
                        # try to swap along Kempe chain (target_color, c)
                        swapped = kempe_swap(new_coloring, target_color, c)
                        if swapped is not None:
                            # check if v changed color
                            if swapped[v] != target_color:
                                new_coloring = swapped
                                changed = True
                                verts.remove(v)
                                break
                    if changed:
                        break
                if changed:
                    coloring = new_coloring
            # after trying to recolor all verts, if none left, we can drop the color
            if not any(coloring[i] == target_color for i in range(n)):
                # compact colors
                coloring = compact_colors(coloring)
                # restart reduction with new coloring
                return reduce_kempe(coloring)
        return coloring
    # Generate candidates
    candidates = []
    candidates.append(dsatur())
    candidates.append(rlf())
    candidates.append(smallest_last())
    # Choose best (fewest colors)
    best = None
    best_colors = float('inf')
    for col in candidates:
        if not is_proper(col):
            continue
        cols = num_colors(col)
        if cols < best_colors:
            best_colors = cols
            best = col
    if best is None:
        # fallback: greedy by degree order
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda u: len(adj_list[u]), reverse=True)
        color = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:

            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):

            color[v] = c
        best = color
    # Apply Kempe reduction
    best = reduce_kempe(best)
    # Ensure proper and compact
    if not is_proper(best):
        # last resort: DSATUR
        best = dsatur()
    best = compact_colors(best)
    return best

            for v in neighbors[u]:

        mapping = {}

                mapping[c] = next_color
                next_color += 1
            coloring[i] = mapping[c]

        for row in adj:
            for val in row:
                if val not in (0, 1):
                    all_binary = False
                    break
            if not all_binary:
                break
        if all_binary:
            is_matrix = True

    # Convert to adjacency list and compute bitmask adjacency
    if is_matrix:
        adj_list = []
        for i in range(n):
            neighbors = []
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1:
                    neighbors.append(j)
            adj_list.append(neighbors)
    else:
        adj_list = adj

    # Build bitmask adjacency for fast operations
    bit_adj = [0] * n
    for u in range(n):
        mask = 0
        for v in adj_list[u]:
            mask |= (1 << v)
        bit_adj[u] = mask

    # Helper: check if coloring is valid
    def is_valid_coloring(colors):
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and colors[u] == colors[v]:
                    return False
        return True

    # Helper: number of colors used
    def num_colors(colors):
        if not colors:
            return 0
        return max(colors) + 1

    # Helper: normalize colors to 0..k-1
    def normalize(colors):
        if not colors:
            return colors
        mapping = {}
        next_color = 0
        for c in colors:
            if c not in mapping:
                mapping[c] = next_color
                next_color += 1

        colored = 0
        # Order: we will select vertices one by one
        for _ in range(n):
            # Select uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree in uncolored subgraph
            best_v = -1
            best_sat = -1
            best_deg = -1
            for v in range(n):
                if colors[v] != -1:
                    continue
                sat = saturation[v].bit_count()

                uncolored_neighbors = 0
                for nb in adj_list[v]:
                    if colors[nb] == -1:
                        uncolored_neighbors += 1
                if sat > best_sat or (sat == best_sat and uncolored_neighbors > best_deg) or \
                   (sat == best_sat and uncolored_neighbors == best_deg and v < best_v):
                    best_sat = sat
                    best_deg = uncolored_neighbors
                    best_v = v
            v = best_v
            # Find smallest available color
            used = saturation[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[v] = c

            for nb in adj_list[v]:
                if colors[nb] == -1:  # only update uncolored neighbors

    def rlf():

        color = 0

        uncolored = [True] * n
        uncolored_count = n

            # Build independent set for this color
            S = []  # vertices to color with current color
            # Step 1: pick vertex with max degree in uncolored subgraph
            best_v = -1
            best_deg = -1

                    continue

                for nb in adj_list[v]:
                    if uncolored[nb]:
                        deg += 1
                if deg > best_deg:
                    best_deg = deg
                    best_v = v
            if best_v == -1:  # should not happen
                break
            S.append(best_v)
            uncolored[best_v] = False
            uncolored_count -= 1
            # Partition: U = vertices not adjacent to any in S (eligible), W = adjacent to S (ineligible)
            # We'll maintain U as a list and W as a boolean array for fast lookup
            in_W = [False] * n
            # Mark neighbors of S as ineligible (W)
            for u in S:
                for nb in adj_list[u]:
                    if uncolored[nb]:
                        in_W[nb] = True
            # U: uncolored and not in W
            U = [v for v in range(n) if uncolored[v] and not in_W[v]]
            # While U not empty
            while U:
                # Select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_deg_U = -1  # for tie-break: min degree in U
                for u in U:

                    score = 0
                    for nb in adj_list[u]:

                    deg_U = 0
                    for nb in adj_list[u]:
                        if uncolored[nb] and not in_W[nb]:  # nb in U
                            deg_U += 1
                    if score > best_score or (score == best_score and deg_U < best_deg_U) or \
                       (score == best_score and deg_U == best_deg_U and u < best_u):
                        best_score = score
                        best_deg_U = deg_U
                        best_u = u
                u = best_u
                # Add u to S
                S.append(u)
                uncolored[u] = False
                uncolored_count -= 1
                # Remove u from U
                U.remove(u)
                # Move neighbors of u from U to W
                for nb in adj_list[u]:
                    if uncolored[nb] and not in_W[nb]:  # nb was in U
                        in_W[nb] = True
                        # Remove nb from U if present
                        if nb in U:
                            U.remove(nb)
            # Assign color to all in S
            for v in S:
                colors[v] = color
            color += 1

    # Smallest-Last ordering (Matula & Beck)
    def smallest_last():
        # Compute degeneracy ordering by repeatedly removing min degree vertex
        # We'll work on a copy of degrees and adjacency
        deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        # List of vertices, we will remove them
        removed = [False] * n
        order = []  # removal order
        # We need to update degrees as we remove vertices
        # Use bucket sort for efficiency (since n <= 100, we can do O(n^2))
        for _ in range(n):

            min_deg = float('inf')

            for v in range(n):

                    min_deg = deg[v]
                    v_min = v

            order.append(v_min)
            # Decrease degree of neighbors
            for nb in adj_list[v_min]:

                    deg[nb] -= 1

        colors = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for nb in adj_list[v]:
                if colors[nb] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << colors[nb])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[v] = c

    def kempe_reduce(colors):

        col = colors[:]

        # Try to reduce colors as long as possible
        improved = True
        while improved and k > 1:
            improved = False
            # Target the last color (k-1)
            target_color = k - 1

            target_vertices = [v for v in range(n) if col[v] == target_color]

            for v in target_vertices:

                for c in range(target_color):

                    # but after swap, we want to free the target_color for v (i.e., v becomes c, and no vertex becomes target_color)
                    # However, if the component contains another target_color vertex, swapping would move that vertex to target_color,
                    # so we don't free the color. We need a component that contains v and no other target_color vertex? 
                    # Actually, we can allow multiple target_color vertices in the component as long as after swap, 
                    # none of them remain target_color? Let's think:

                    # So the number of target_color vertices in the component becomes y.
                    # To free the color globally, we need that after swap, there are zero target_color vertices.
                    # That means we need y = 0 (no c-colored vertices in the component) and then after swap, 
                    # the x target_color vertices become c, and 0 vertices become target_color.
                    # But if there is at least one c-colored vertex in the component, then after swap we get at least one target_color vertex.
                    # Therefore, we can only eliminate the color if we find a Kempe chain (component) that contains v and has no c-colored vertices.
                    # Then after swapping, all target_color vertices in the component become c, and no vertex becomes target_color.
                    # So we need to check: in the subgraph induced by colors {target_color, c}, the connected component containing v 
                    # must have no vertex of color c.
                    # However, note that v is target_color, so if there is any c-colored vertex in the component, then the component has both colors.
                    # We want the component to have only target_color vertices (i.e., an isolated set of target_color vertices with no adjacent c-colored vertices).
                    # That is equivalent to: v has no neighbor of color c? Not exactly: because the component could be larger via target_color vertices.
                    # Example: v -- u (both target_color) and u has a neighbor w of color c -> then the component includes w (c) via u.
                    # So we need to do a BFS/DFS over the component and check that we never see color c.
                    from collections import deque
                    visited = [False] * n
                    queue = deque([v])
                    visited[v] = True
                    has_c = False
                    comp_target = []  # target_color vertices in component
                    while queue:
                        x = queue.popleft()
                        if col[x] == target_color:
                            comp_target.append(x)
                        elif col[x] == c:
                            has_c = True

                        for nb in adj_list[x]:
                            if not visited[nb] and (col[nb] == target_color or col[nb] == c):
                                visited[nb] = True

                    if not has_c:
                        # We can swap: all target_color vertices in component become c, and no vertex becomes target_color
                        for x in comp_target:

    best_k = float('inf')

    for func in [dsatur, rlf, smallest_last]:
        try:
            cols = func()
            if not is_valid_coloring(cols):

                continue
            k = num_colors(cols)
            if k < best_k:
                best_k = k
                best_colors = cols
        except Exception:
            continue

    # If none worked, fall back to greedy (should not happen)
    if best_colors is None:
        # Simple greedy in order 0..n-1
        colors = [-1] * n
        for i in range(n):
            used = 0
            for nb in adj_list[i]:
                if colors[nb] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << colors[nb])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[i] = c

    # Apply Kempe reduction to try to improve
    best_colors = kempe_reduce(best_colors)

    if not is_valid_coloring(best_colors):

        colors = [-1] * n

            for nb in adj_list[i]:
                if colors[nb] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << colors[nb])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[i] = c
        best_colors = normalize(colors)
    else:
        best_colors = normalize(best_colors)

    return best_colors

    def greedy_color(order):

            for u in neighbors[v]:

                    used.add(color[u])
            c = 0

            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: (deg_sub[x], random.random()))
            independent_set = {v}

            U = uncolored - {v} - neighbors[v]

            while U:

                def score(u):

                    u_deg = len(neighbors[u] & U)
                    return (w_count, -u_deg, random.random())
                u = max(U, key=score)
                independent_set.add(u)

        for _ in range(n):

            while ptr <= max_deg and not buckets[ptr]:

            if ptr > max_deg:

            for u in neighbors[v]:

                    old_deg = deg[u]
                    buckets[old_deg].remove(u)

                    if new_deg <= max_deg:

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

                    all_binary = False
                    break

            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1:
                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
                    neighbors[i].append(j)
    else:  # adjacency list
        for i in range(n):
            for j in adj[i]:
                bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
                neighbors[i].append(j)

    # Helper: count bits in integer
    def bit_count(x: int) -> int:
        return x.bit_count()

    # DSATUR algorithm
    def dsatur() -> list[int]:
        color = [-1] * n
        # Saturation: for each vertex, bitmask of colors used by colored neighbors
        sat = [0] * n
        # Degree in uncolored subgraph (initially full degree)
        deg_uncolored = [bit_count(bit_adj[i]) for i in range(n)]
        uncolored = set(range(n))

        for _ in range(n):
            # Select vertex with max saturation, tie-break by max deg_uncolored, then min index
            v = -1
            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                s = bit_count(sat[u])
                d = deg_uncolored[u]
                if s > max_sat or (s == max_sat and (d > max_deg or (d == max_deg and u < v))):
                    max_sat = s
                    max_deg = d
                    v = u

            used = sat[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1

                else:

            # W = {u in uncolored \ S : at least one edge to S}
            U = set()
            W = set()
            for u in uncolored:
                if u in S:
                    continue
                if bit_adj[u] & sum((1 << w) for w in S):
                    W.add(u)
                else:
                    U.add(u)

            while U:
                # Select u in U maximizing |N(u) ∩ W|, tie-break by min degree in G[U]
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_deg_U = float('inf')
                for u in U:

                    score = bit_count(bit_adj[u] & sum((1 << w) for w in W))

                    deg_U = bit_count(bit_adj[u] & sum((1 << w) for w in U))

                        best_deg_U = deg_U

            for u in neighbors[v]:

    try:

    try:

    # Select candidate with minimal number of colors
    def num_colors(col):

    # Kempe chain color reduction
    def kempe_reduction(color_in: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        color = color_in[:]
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            # Find smallest color class (largest color index that is used)
            # We try to eliminate the highest color index first
            max_color = max(color) if color else -1
            for target in range(max_color, -1, -1):
                # Collect vertices with color == target
                verts = [v for v in range(n) if color[v] == target]
                if not verts:

                    for u in neighbors[v]:

                            used |= (1 << color[u])

                        # We want to see if we can swap in the component of v to free target for v
                        # Actually, we want to move v to color c: if in the (target, c) Kempe chain of v,
                        # the color c is not present in the neighborhood of v, we can swap.
                        # Standard: if there is no path from v to any vertex of color c using only colors target and c,
                        # then we can swap target and c in the component of v, making v color c.
                        # But easier: if v is not adjacent to any vertex of color c, we already handled above.
                        # So we need to check if v is adjacent to a vertex of color c? Actually, if it is,

                            x = q.popleft()

                                    if y not in comp:
                                        comp.add(y)

                        # So v's neighbors: if a neighbor is in comp and was color c, after swap it becomes target -> ok.
                        # If a neighbor is in comp and was color target, after swap it becomes c -> conflict if neighbor is adjacent to v.
                        # Actually, we need: after swap, no neighbor of v has color c.
                        # Neighbors of v that are in comp: if they were color target, become c -> conflict.
                        # Neighbors of v that are in comp: if they were color c, become target -> no conflict (since v becomes c? wait v becomes c, neighbor becomes target -> ok).
                        # Neighbors of v not in comp: keep their color.
                        # So conflict if there exists a neighbor u of v such that:
                        #   u in comp and color[u] == target (because after swap, u becomes c, and v becomes c -> same color)
                        #   or u not in comp and color[u] == c (because after swap, v becomes c, u stays c)
                        conflict = False
                        for u in neighbors[v]:
                            if color[u] == c and u not in comp:
                                conflict = True
                                break
                            if color[u] == target and u in comp:
                                conflict = True
                                break
                        if not conflict:
                            # Perform swap: in comp, swap target <-> c
                            for x in comp:
                                if color[x] == target:
                                    color[x] = c
                                elif color[x] == c:
                                    color[x] = target
                            changed = True
                            break
                    if changed:
                        break
                if changed:
                    break
            if changed:
                break  # restart while changed loop
        # Compact colors: remap to 0..k-1
        # Map used colors to consecutive integers
        used_colors = sorted(set(color))
        mapping = {old: new for new, old in enumerate(used_colors)}
        color = [mapping[c] for c in color]
        return color

    best = kempe_reduction(best)
    return best

            q_i = q[i]
            max_val = 0
            for m in range(M):
                val = f[m] + q_i[m]
                if val > max_val:
                    max_val = val
            makespans[i] = max_val
        return makespans

    # NEH construction with Taillard acceleration
    def neh_construction():
        # Job order by total processing time descending
        order = sorted(range(N), key=lambda i: total_proc[i], reverse=True)
        # Start with first two jobs
        if N >= 2:
            # Evaluate both orders
            ms01 = makespan([order[0], order[1]])
            ms10 = makespan([order[1], order[0]])
            if ms01 <= ms10:
                perm = [order[0], order[1]]
            else:
                perm = [order[1], order[0]]
            start_k = 2
        else:
            perm = [order[0]]
            start_k = 1
        # Insert remaining jobs
        for k in range(start_k, N):
            job = order[k]
            ms_list = taillard_insertion_eval(perm, k, job)
            # Find position with minimal makespan (break ties by earliest)
            best_pos = 0
            best_ms = ms_list[0]
            for pos in range(1, k+1):
                if ms_list[pos] < best_ms:
                    best_ms = ms_list[pos]
                    best_pos = pos
            perm.insert(best_pos, job)
        return perm

    # Iterated Greedy metaheuristic
    def iterated_greedy(initial_perm):
        # Parameters
        d = 3 if N >= 3 else N  # destruction size
        T_param = 0.5
        total_processing = sum(total_proc)
        T = T_param * total_processing / (10 * N * M) if N * M > 0 else 1e-6

        curr_ms = makespan(curr_perm)
        best_perm = curr_perm[:]
        best_ms = curr_ms

        lb = 0
        for m in range(M):
            min_pre = min(proc[i][:m] for i in range(N)) if m > 0 else [0]*N
            min_suf = min(proc[i][m+1:] for i in range(N)) if m < M-1 else [0]*N
            sum_pre = [sum(min_pre[i]) for i in range(N)] if m > 0 else [0]*N
            sum_suf = [sum(min_suf[i]) for i in range(N)] if m < M-1 else [0]*N
            lb_m = min(sum_pre) + sum(proc[i][m] for i in range(N)) + min(sum_suf)
            if lb_m > lb:
                lb = lb_m
        # If initial solution already hits lower bound, return
        if best_ms == lb:
            return best_perm
        # Main loop: aim for ~40-80 iterations within time budget
        max_iters = 60
        for _ in range(max_iters):
            # Destruction: remove d random jobs
            indices = list(range(N))
            random.shuffle(indices)
            removed_indices = indices[:d]
            removed_jobs = [curr_perm[i] for i in removed_indices]
            # Build destruction sequence (remaining jobs in original order)
            dest_set = set(removed_indices)
            pi_D = [curr_perm[i] for i in range(N) if i not in dest_set]
            # Reconstruction: reinsert removed jobs one by one in random order
            random.shuffle(removed_jobs)
            for job in removed_jobs:
                k = len(pi_D)
                ms_list = taillard_insertion_eval(pi_D, k, job)
                best_pos = 0
                best_ms_insert = ms_list[0]
                for pos in range(1, k+1):
                    if ms_list[pos] < best_ms_insert:
                        best_ms_insert = ms_list[pos]
                        best_pos = pos
                pi_D.insert(best_pos, job)
            new_perm = pi_D
            new_ms = makespan(new_perm)
            # Acceptance criterion
            if new_ms < curr_ms:
                curr_perm = new_perm
                curr_ms = new_ms
                if new_ms < best_ms:
                    best_perm = new_perm[:]
                    best_ms = new_ms
                    if best_ms == lb:
                        break
            else:
                if curr_ms > 0:
                    prob = math.exp(-(new_ms - curr_ms) / T)
                else:
                    prob = 0.0
                if random.random() < prob:
                    curr_perm = new_perm
                    curr_ms = new_ms
        return best_perm

    # Run NEH construction followed by IG refinement
    initial_perm = neh_construction()
    return iterated_greedy(initial_perm)

    return best_perm

def schedule_flowshop(times: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

            for m in range(1, M):
                t[m] = max(t[m-1], t[m]) + pt[m]
        return t[-1]

    def forward_matrix(seq):
        k = len(seq)
        if k == 0:
            return [[0]*M]
        e = [[0]*M for _ in range(k)]
        for r in range(k):
            job = seq[r]
            pt = job_times[job]
            if r == 0:
                e[0][0] = pt[0]
                for m in range(1, M):
                    e[0][m] = e[0][m-1] + pt[m]
            else:
                e[r][0] = e[r-1][0] + pt[0]
                for m in range(1, M):
                    e[r][m] = max(e[r-1][m], e[r][m-1]) + pt[m]
        return e
    
    # Taillard's acceleration: backward tail matrix for a given sequence
    def backward_matrix(seq):
        k = len(seq)
        if k == 0:
            return [[0]*M]
        q = [[0]*M for _ in range(k+1)]
        # q[k][m] = 0 already by initialization
        for r in range(k-1, -1, -1):
            job = seq[r]
            pt = job_times[job]
            q[r][M-1] = q[r+1][M-1] + pt[M-1]
            for m in range(M-2, -1, -1):
                q[r][m] = max(q[r+1][m], q[r][m+1]) + pt[m]
        return q
    
    # Evaluate makespan for inserting job x at position i in current seq using Taillard's O(M) method
    def insertion_cost(seq, x, i, e_prev, q_prev):
        # e_prev: forward matrix for seq (length k), q_prev: backward matrix for seq (length k)
        k = len(seq)

            for m in range(1, M):

        else:
            e_im1 = e_prev[i-1]  # e[i-1][:]
            pt = job_times[x]
            f[0] = e_im1[0] + pt[0]
            for m in range(1, M):
                f[m] = max(f[m-1], e_im1[m]) + pt[m]

        for m in range(M):
            val = f[m] + q_i[m]
            if val > max_val:
                max_val = val

        else:
            seq = seq2

        for k in range(2, N):
            job = order[k]

            best_cost = float('inf')

            e_mat = forward_matrix(seq)
            q_mat = backward_matrix(seq)

                cost = insertion_cost(seq, job, i, e_mat, q_mat)
                if cost < best_cost:
                    best_cost = cost
                    best_pos = i
            # Insert job at best_pos
            seq.insert(best_pos, job)
        return seq
    
    # Iterated Greedy with Taillard-accelerated reconstruction
    def iterated_greedy(initial_seq):

        d = 3  # destruction size

        best_seq = initial_seq[:]
        best_makespan = makespan(initial_seq)
        
        # Precompute LB for early exit (optional, not always tight)
        # We'll skip LB calculation for speed; rely on iteration limit

        for _ in range(max_iter):
            # Destruction: remove d random jobs

                removed = current_seq[:]

                indices.sort(reverse=True)
                removed = []
                for idx in indices:
                    removed.append(current_seq.pop(idx))
                destroyed = current_seq  # remaining sequence
            
            # Reconstruction: reinsert removed jobs one by one in random order
            random.shuffle(removed)
            for job in removed:
                best_pos = 0
                best_cost = float('inf')
                # Precompute forward and backward matrices for current destroyed seq
                e_mat = forward_matrix(destroyed)
                q_mat = backward_matrix(destroyed)
                k = len(destroyed)
                for i in range(k+1):  # positions 0..k
                    cost = insertion_cost(destroyed, job, i, e_mat, q_mat)
                    if cost < best_cost:
                        best_cost = cost
                        best_pos = i
                destroyed.insert(best_pos, job)
            
            new_seq = destroyed
            new_makespan = makespan(new_seq)
            
            # Acceptance criterion
            if new_makespan < makespan(current_seq):
                current_seq = new_seq
                if new_makespan < best_makespan:
                    best_seq = new_seq[:]
                    best_makespan = new_makespan
            else:
                # Metropolis acceptance
                delta = new_makespan - makespan(current_seq)
                if random.random() < math.exp(-delta / T):
                    current_seq = new_seq
        
        return best_seq
    
    # Build initial solution with NEH
    init_seq = neh_construction()
    # Refine with Iterated Greedy
    result_seq = iterated_greedy(init_seq)
    return result_seq

        indices = random.sample(range(N), d)
        removed_set = set(indices)
        destroyed = [current[i] for i in range(N) if i not in removed_set]
        removed_jobs = [current[i] for i in indices]
        random.shuffle(removed_jobs)
        # reconstruction: reinsert each job using Taillard-accelerated NEH insertion
        for job in removed_jobs:
            destroyed = insert_job(destroyed, job)
        # acceptance
        new_mk = makespan(destroyed)
        if new_mk < makespan(current) or random.random() < math.exp(-(new_mk - makespan(current)) / T):
            current = destroyed
            if new_mk < best_mk:
                best = current[:]
                best_mk = new_mk
    return best
